title: Provisioning intake adjudicator, autoscale signal harmonization, and capacity commitment simulator
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Build a single adjudication surface and simulation tool for Dedicated provisioning requests that (1) harmonizes autoscale policy suggestions with requested throughput guarantees and latency SLOs, (2) surfaces a recommended capacity commitment and cost estimate, and (3) provides audit-friendly decision logs for approvals.

Background: Current intake is fragmented: sales/solutions, support, and self-serve requests arrive with different fields and teams manually translate them into capacity commitments. This causes inconsistent SLA promises, late provisioning, and surprise cost overruns. We need an adjudicator service + UI that standardizes signals (throughput_profile, peak_pattern, latency_slo, budget_limit, priority_bucket) and runs a simulator to estimate run-rate, unit cost, and warm-up provisioning time under autoscale policies.

Goals:
- Standardize request schema and scoring for automated pre-approval lanes.
- Provide autoscale policy harmonization: map request signals to one of the recommended policy templates (steady-reserve, burst-buffered, on-demand-fallback) and show trade-offs.
- Build a simulator that projects throughput, latency risk, and monthly cost across a 90-day horizon for candidate commitments.
- Create an adjudicator UI for operations and commercial reviewers that shows suggested decision, supporting rationale, and one-click approve/deny/needs-info flows.

Out of scope:
- New billing system changes (we will surface estimated cost only).
- Rewriting autoscaler runtime; we will generate policy artifacts compatible with the existing autoscale engine.

Stakeholders: Commercial (Megan Ruiz), Solutions Eng (Aaron Tang), Runtime (Liam O'Connor), Reliability (Elena Park), Security & Compliance (Noah Chen).
acceptance_criteria: Intake API v1 accepts standardized fields: throughput_profile, peak_pattern, latency_slo_ms, cost_budget_usd_month, priority_bucket, requested_start_date
Automated scorer assigns one of: auto-approved, requires-review, blocked based on configurable rules and historical risk models
Autoscale policy recommender returns a named policy plus rationale and estimated 95th percentile latency under simulated load
Simulator produces a 90-day projection: expected monthly tokens, estimated spend, peak utilization, and warm-up time for chosen policy
Adjudicator UI lists pending requests, shows recommended action, allows approver to change policy, add conditions, and record decision with audit log
Decisions are recorded to audit logs with structured reasons and linked to an incident/PR if rollback required

End-to-end acceptance test exists in staging that creates a request, simulates traffic, and verifies that autoscale policy artifact can be applied to the existing autoscale engine without schema changes
